clue.text: Short pause, the minimum of rest?

definitions.meaning: a brief stop to get your wind back
a playful second reading: the smallest amount of rest you can take, just long enough to draw breath

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe the same thing; the question mark flags the jokier second reading of a tiny rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief pause to recover one's wind is the standard colloquial sense of the word.

clue.text: One who uses brass for taps

definitions.text: One who uses brass for taps

parts.words: One who uses brass for taps
parts.note: taps is the bugle call sounded at military funerals and lights-out, played on a brass instrument, not water taps or tap-dancing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taps' tempts towards plumbing or tap-dancing, and 'brass' towards money; here it is the instrument and the evening call.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle player sounds the call named Taps on a brass instrument, so this describes that musician.

clue.text: Times supporting European liberal, for instance

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath the one it holds up

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
liberal in the sense of generous or plentiful, as in a liberal helping, means ample

explanation.surface: A newspaper backing a European liberal politician is cited as a case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign X, placed below E because 'supporting' in a down clue means underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance and an example are synonyms: both mean a single case illustrating something.

clue.text: Give a rocket as transport for mission

parts.note: to take something somewhere is to transport it
for, in the sense of towards or bound for, gives to
a mission is an assigned task

explanation.surface: A rocket is offered as the means of carrying a space mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a rocket' is British slang for a severe telling-off, not a space launch.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a rocket is British slang for scolding them sharply, which is what rebuking means.

clue.text: Dire prospects destroyed group solidarity

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Grim outlook ruined the team's sense of togetherness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges the thirteen letters of DIRE PROSPECTS.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing names the shared pride and loyalty binding members of a team, i.e. group morale.

clue.text: Greek character repeatedly stylish, affectedly so

indicators.note: repeatedly tells us to write the letter name twice in a row

parts.note: chi is the twenty-second letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person is described as always fashionable, in a showy way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' looks like a person but is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes pretentious, fussy elegance: smart but self-consciously so.

clue.text: Crude cutting from journalist

definitions.meaning: to chop roughly, as with an axe
a writer for a newspaper, especially a jobbing one

explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is just a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to chop roughly and a jobbing newspaper writer, two separate senses.

clue.text: Break arranged as a cure

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rest from work is set up as a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges AS A CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry this term is the pause or break in the middle of a line of verse.

clue.text: Old sources for writing bringing home royalty to novelist

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
K is the abbreviation for king, a royal
H. G. Wells wrote The Time Machine and The War of the Worlds

explanation.surface: An author gets a royal title brought to his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing' and 'to' just join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Pens were once dipped in small pots of ink set into desks, the source of ink for writing.

clue.text: Resort area

parts.note: to resort to a place is to go there

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a holiday region, while 'Resort' as a verb gives GO and 'area' gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian coastal state is famous for its beach holiday destinations, a classic resort area.

clue.text: Controlled, like king continuously on the move?

definitions.text: like king continuously on the move?
definitions.meaning: in chess a king that keeps being attacked must keep moving, staying under attack

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is chess: a king repeatedly threatened is forced to move each turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something back or restrain it is the idiomatic sense; the chess reading literally describes a threatened king.

clue.text: Imprison a Latino improperly crossing borders

parts.note: to intern someone is to confine them, especially in wartime

indicators.note: improperly means not in the right way, so these letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A Latin American is unjustly jailed while passing between countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improperly' looks like a comment on the jailing but signals the anagram, giving ATIONAL; 'crossing borders' is the definition, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spanning several nations goes across national frontiers.

clue.text: Write at length about queen in exile

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to expatiate is to speak or write at great length on a subject
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Someone writes extensively about a queen who has been banished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of' but puts the first piece around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living outside their native country is an exile, the noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Lower classes entertaining this country's noble

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification of occupations
UK, the United Kingdom, the country of this British newspaper

explanation.surface: The working classes are hosting a British aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: D and E are the bottom two bands of the British social grading scale used in market research.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the highest rank of the British peerage, so a nobleman.

clue.text: In various ports, we arbitrate informal suits

indicators.note: In tells us the answer is contained within the following words

explanation.surface: Someone settles disputes in several harbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the letters are concealed inside 'various ports, we arbitrate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracksuits and the like are casual clothes; 'suits' plays on formal business suits.

clue.text: Proverbial vices, for example, awful pet had

indicators.note: awful means dreadful, so these letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: My pet has terrible habits, the proverbial vices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges PET HAD. The seven deadly sins make a group of seven.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of seven, and the seven deadly sins are the proverbial set of vices.

clue.text: Archangel responsible for many religious works

definitions.meaning: one of the archangels named in scripture, alongside Michael and Gabriel
the Renaissance painter of many Madonnas and other sacred pictures

explanation.walkthrough: The same name belongs to the archangel and the Italian Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is borne both by an archangel and by the Renaissance painter of many Madonnas.

clue.text: A sign of penitence accepted by saint, namely

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by, so the saint holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a cilice is a hair shirt worn as penance

explanation.surface: A saint takes on a token of repentance, that is to say.
explanation.walkthrough: A cilice is a rough hair shirt worn to show penitence; it goes inside ST.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin term, abbreviated sc., means 'that is to say', introducing a clarification.

clue.text: Quintessential cooling drink in small volume

indicators.note: in places the drink inside the measure

parts.note: cc, a cubic centimetre, is a small unit of volume
lassi is a chilled Indian yoghurt drink

explanation.surface: A refreshing drink served in a tiny measure is the perfect example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooling' is not a temperature instruction but part of describing an Indian yoghurt drink; cc is the cubic centimetre.
explanation.definitionFit: Typical or exemplary, the very model of its kind: a synonym of quintessential.

clue.text: Where some journalists work on some The winn occasions

clue.text: Quarrels, for example, mostly are just that

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: just that refers back to quarrels, read in its everyday sense of rows or arguments

explanation.surface: Arguments, for instance, are mostly exactly that.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarrels here are crossbow bolts; 'just that' points back to the clue's first word taken in its everyday sense of arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is the short bolt shot from a crossbow, an example of the missiles shot from bows.

clue.text: Having bought it after the sell-by date?

definitions.text: Having bought it after the sell-by date?

parts.words: Having bought it after the sell-by date?
parts.note: to have bought it is slang for having died; read as a shopper it means arriving after the date, i.e. tardy

explanation.walkthrough: 'bought it' is slang for died, and the word means both dead and overdue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both deceased and arriving after the due time, the two senses the clue plays on.

clue.text: Be creative with British cats and dogs

parts.note: raining cats and dogs means pouring heavily, as in a downpour

explanation.walkthrough: 'cats and dogs' looks like pets but alludes to the idiom for heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate ideas freely, often in a group, is the verb's sense: a way of being inventive.

clue.text: State spelt without a consonant, listener might conclude

definitions.text: State spelt without a consonant, listener might conclude

parts.words: State spelt without a consonant, listener might conclude
parts.note: a US state whose spoken name sounds like nothing but vowels, so someone hearing it might guess there is no consonant in the spelling

explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud the name sounds like three vowel sounds; written, it has one consonant.
explanation.definitionFit: This Midwestern US state's spoken name sounds like a run of vowels alone.

clue.text: House seen in need of conversion, to be realistic

parts.note: the House of Commons, the lower chamber of the UK Parliament

indicators.note: conversion means changing form, so these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A building is noticed to need renovation, to be practical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in need of conversion' signals the anagram, giving ENSE; the House is Britain's House of Commons, the elected chamber of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the phrase means sensible and practical, a close synonym of realistic.

clue.text: Badly reduced state

definitions.meaning: .... is the shortened form of Illinois, a US state

explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced state' is a US state name cut down to its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means poorly or badly, and is also the short form of Illinois.

clue.text: Soldier in volunteer force who explored Pacific

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve; with the possessive 's it gives TA's, so a soldier in it is the TA's man
man is a common word for an ordinary soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in a reserve force went exploring the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's volunteer reserve; a soldier in it is the TA's man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch navigator Abel Tasman explored the Pacific, discovering Tasmania and New Zealand.

clue.text: Completely one-sided, yet fair

parts.note: all means wholly or completely, as in all alone
right is one side, as opposed to left

explanation.surface: Something entirely biased is nonetheless said to be just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yet' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfactory or acceptable, middling but fine, is what fair means here.
